turn_prompts:
Read validation_environment_contract before writing files. In the authoring workspace, source/ is a read-only reference and task/ is the only writable candidate directory; write exactly instruction.md, task.toml, environment/Dockerfile, solution/solve.sh, tests/test.sh, and tests_analysis.json under task/. Only provision Debian packages in environment/Dockerfile when the frozen task genuinely requires them. Whenever apt-get is used, switch the default Debian APT sources from HTTP to HTTPS before apt-get update exactly with this guarded command. Bookworm images may ship either /etc/apt/sources.list or deb822 /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources; a missing file must never fail the build:
RUN if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then sed -i 's|^deb http://|deb https://|; s|^deb-src http://|deb-src https://|' /etc/apt/sources.list; fi; for f in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then sed -i 's|^URIs: http://|URIs: https://|' "$f"; fi; done
Never use sed alternation or \1 backreference expressions for this switch; the controlled build network permits HTTPS egress only. Call harbor_validate_candidate for structured diagnostics; submit no candidate bytes in prose. Work efficiently: web search and general internet access are unavailable and must never be attempted. Do not perform open-ended repository exploration; make only the targeted reads needed to write the candidate, then write every candidate file and call harbor_validate_candidate within this same turn. task.toml must be the Harbor 0.18 TaskConfig TOML with the [metadata], [task], [environment], and [verifier] tables: [metadata] defines code_lang, task_type, application, is_0_to_1, github_url, and commit_id (the last two matching the frozen repository and commit); [task] defines a valid org/name name and a non-empty description; [environment] defines positive build_timeout_sec, network_mode = "no-network", and workdir = "/workspace/source"; [verifier] defines positive timeout_sec. tests_analysis.json must be the strict harbor.standard-authoring-tests-analysis.v2 JSON object: format "harbor.standard-authoring-tests-analysis.v2", version "2", one or more unique requirement_ids (each starts with an uppercase letter and continues with A-Z, 0-9, _ or -), and non-empty provided_information (what the instruction and environment already provide), theoretical_path (the model’s theoretical pass path), and passing_evidence (the objective pass conditions).

Validator runtime uses --network none and a read-only root filesystem; /source and /task are read-only, and /work is a fresh writable copy of /source. solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh must operate on /work through HARBOR_WORKSPACE, never write source/ or /source. For Rust/Cargo browser-wasm tasks, install generic wasm/browser tools in environment/Dockerfile, rely only on pinned base-image, repository-vendored, or frozen-input dependencies at runtime, and set CARGO_HOME=/work/.cargo-home and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/work/.cargo-target instead of copying full Cargo registry/target caches into limited /tmp.

Use the same fenced workspace to correct only diagnostics bound to the candidate and frozen VerificationContract. When that contract invokes test.sh through sh, both test.sh and solution/solve.sh must be POSIX sh compatible: do not use set -o pipefail, bash arrays, [[, or other Bash-only syntax. Call harbor_validate_candidate with a passing candidate; the host captures the immutable snapshot.
